newsitem.title: HONG KONG: GITIC Enterprises IPO seen over 900X subscribed.
newsitem.headline: GITIC Enterprises IPO seen over 900X subscribed.

text.p: GITIC Enterprises Ltd's much anticipated initial public offering (IPO) has likely become Hong Kong's most popular ever, with market sources saying on Thursday they expecting it to be between 900 and 1,000 times subscribed.
The subscription period for the IPO closed on Thursday and despite talk this week the offering had hit a snag, investors had flocked to get their hands on the shares, the sources said.
"It's certain that the subscription level will be the highest ever," said a source close to the underwriters.

GITIC Enterprises imports and sells construction materials in Hong Kong and China, and also owns the second floor of a shopping mall at GITIC Plaza in Guangzhou in China's southern province of Guangdong.
The company offered 100 million new shares at HK$1.05 each.
Dealing in the shares is due to begin on March 26. The company said it will reveal subscription results on March 24.
Rumours spread in the market on Tuesday the company may not have obtained all necessary approvals for the float from the China Securities Regulation Commission, brokers said.
But the company, which is backed by the Guangdong provincial government, said on Wednesday its Hong Kong IPO and listing plan would proceed on schedule. It did not clarify the rumours.
Some sources said they did not rule out the possibility some people were spreading the rumours in an attempt to cool strong speculative demand for the issue.
Analysts said the saga could dampen speculative demand for red chips, which are usually buoyed by hopes their Chinese parents will inject quality assets.
If mainland regulators began to take a heavy-handed approach, it may make it harder for red chips to draw in new assets, they said.
"Investors may take a cautious attitude towards other upcoming new listings of the same kind," said one executive at a local brokerage.
One corporate finance source said merchant bankers may also take extra precautions in obtaining approvals when they prepare listings.
Analysts said GITIC Enterprises had benefited from strong interest in China plays.
Its small issue size, prospects of future asset injections and ties to its parent -- one of the main financial institutions in Guangdong -- had made the issue particularly attractive.

GITIC Enterprises is indirectly controlled by the Guangdong provincial goverment's investment arm, Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp (GITIC), which had total assets of about 20.56 billion yuan as at the end of 1995.
Goldwyn Capital Ltd and ABN-AMRO Rothschild are the sponsors and lead underwriters of the issue.
